instruction: Adjust my mouse settings to use natural (smartphone-style) scrolling.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires enabling natural scrolling for mouse via GNOME settings. The setup disables natural-scroll, and the agent must enable it using gsettings command. The evaluator verifies the setting is enabled by reading the gsettings value.
metadata.verification: The evaluator uses existing vm_command_line getter and exact_match metric. Expected output is 'true\n' when the setting is enabled.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly uses vm_command_line getter to read the GNOME natural-scroll setting via gsettings command
The exact_match metric is appropriate for verifying boolean settings represented as strings
Expected value 'true\n' correctly represents the enabled state in gsettings output format
Complete coverage: evaluator checks the single requirement (enabling natural scrolling for mouse)
State is persistent and accessible: gsettings values don't require special UI state or postconfig
Data flow is correct: getter extracts setting value → metric compares to expected 'true\n' → verifies enabled state
No edge case issues: gsettings commands return consistent, reliable output
